the frequency of mutations produced in bacteria by alkylating agents depends on the number of gene copies or chromosome replicating forks present in the cell, and that the dependence is different for different types of mutagens.
the mutation frequency induced by an alkylating agent depends on the average number (a) of replicating chromosome forks per cell and/or the average number (b) of gene copies per cell.
the frequency of mutations in E. coli induced by alkylating agents depends on the number of DNA base al-kylation products formed per cell.

the influence of the number of chromosome replicative forks per cell on the induction of mutations in Escherichiacoli K-12 trp A58 by monofunctional and bifunctional alkylators.
the influence of the physiological state of the cell on the frequency of mutation induced in E. coli by alkylating agents.

the frequency of reversibly induced mutations is influenced by growth rate-dependent changes, but that these changes are not due to growth rate-dependent changes either in the number of chromosome replicons per cell, or in the total amount of DNA per cell.

the frequency of mutation induced in E. coli K-12 is influenced by both the number of gene copies and the number of replicative forks per cell, depending on the type of mutagen used and the base alkylation product formed.

in E. coli K-12 the frequency of reversals induced by alkylating agents is dependent on the average numbers of chromosome replicative forks and gene copies per cell.

the frequency of reversibly induced mutations is dependent on the number of chromosome replicons in the cell, and the number of copies of the target gene in the cell, but that the number of replicons per cell is more important than the number of target gene copies.

the frequency of mutations in trpA58 induced by MMS is proportional to the average number (n) of trpA gene copy per cell, whereas for the other four alkylating agents the frequency of mutations is proportional to n + 1, where n is the average number of DNA replication forks per cell.
